content.text: SynapseNote is a calm place to write, plan and keep what you know. There is no account, no subscription, no AI and no ads, and nothing you write is ever sent anywhere. Every page is a plain Markdown file in a folder you chose, so your notes stay yours even without SynapseNote.
Each chapter below is a real page that shows its feature working. Try things, change them, break them. When you are done, delete this page from its
menu at the top right and every chapter and example goes with it.

Pages are Markdown, canvases are JSON Canvas, databases are folders of pages. Open them in any text editor.
Databases with board, table, calendar, list and gallery views, relations and formulas, all on your own devices.
Links, backlinks, a graph, canvases and daily notes work the moment you open the app. No plugins to hunt for.
No telemetry, no cloud, no AI reading your notes. Lock any page with a password, sync between your own devices over your own network.
A native app for the Mac, the iPad and the iPhone, with the same vault on each.

A database is a page whose subpages are its rows. Each row is a full page with its own content, plus properties like status, dates and numbers. In your vault a database is a folder, and each row is a Markdown file with its properties at the top, readable by any Markdown app.

content.text: Write a line as a question, two colons and an answer, on any page, and it becomes a flashcard.
) shows the cards due today. Grade each one and SynapseNote schedules it again, sooner if you forgot and later if it was easy.
What does SynapseNote never send anywhere? :: Your notes
Which key opens today’s note? :: ⇧ ⌘ D
How do you mention a date? :: Type @ and pick one
Edit the question or answer whenever you like. A card keeps its schedule as long as its question stays the same.

SynapseNote has no servers. It never phones home, has no analytics and no AI. The only time it uses the network is when you ask it to: loading a picture from the web, or syncing with your own devices.
Your notes live in a vault, a normal folder. On a Mac,

in the File menu opens it; on an iPad or an iPhone it is in the Files app. You can edit the files in any app while SynapseNote is open and it follows along. Keep the folder in a backup or a synced drive if you like.
SynapseNote keeps earlier versions of a page as you work. Choose
from the page menu to see what changed, line by line, and bring back any version.
The file on disk becomes unreadable without the password, using AES-256.
Unlock it with the password when you open it, and lock it again from the menu.
If you forget the password, nobody can open the page. Not you, and not SynapseNote.
Deleted pages go to the Trash in the sidebar first, so a slip is never permanent.

and turn on sync on two devices on the same network. Pair them once with the code one of them shows, and from then on they keep each other up to date directly, with no cloud in between. When both change the same page, both versions are kept so nothing is lost.
You can also put the vault folder in any sync service you already trust, such as a synced cloud drive.
